messages.author: 80f00f6e5c28f957
messages.subject: segmentation approach
parts:
I have few questions about segmentation algorithm. I read Wreczycka et al 2017 paper (great job!) and I am now aware of the power of the segmentation approach. I made an attempt to apply it to my data.  I am bit confused the way it is applied though. Seems that you can use it for both diffmeth object or genomic ranges (ie methylome). Do I understand that correctly?  The implication of the segmentation on these two different object is not intuitive to me. Theoretically you can compare different epigenomes (cells) based on that (make their signature) or run methyldiff function between two cell types, run the segmentation of this difference and do annotation. Are both approaches allowed? 

Also, since RRBS is bit biased towards GC, is this not a problem?  I got 3 distinct segments, based on 200 bp windows, on methdiff object and after annotation all 3 segments are in promotor region and I am bit suspicious.  It is not finished yet but make a lot of questions in my head about this technique. Thank you for comments.  Marcin

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] segmentation approach
parts: Hi Marcin,
.  I am bit confused the way it is applied though. Seems that you can use it for both diffmeth object or genomic ranges (ie methylome). Do I understand that correctly?
Yes, if you apply it to DMCs, you would essentially get DMRs that do not have pre-defined lengths. I recommend using this on q-value thresholded DMCs, so no thresholding on methylation difference.

The implication of the segmentation on these two different object is not intuitive to me. Theoretically you can compare different epigenomes (cells) based on that (make their signature) or run methyldiff function between two cell types, run the segmentation of this difference and do annotation. Are both approaches allowed?

segmentation on methylBase objects is similar to the previous applications. You would essentially get 2 to 4 segment classes. the hypo-methylated or lowly methylated segment classes are probably regulatory regions. See Stadler et al. (2009) Nature.

If you run it on methylDiff objects thresholded by q-values, you should get DMRs. This would be similar to other DMR approaches such as eDMR package.

Also, since RRBS is bit biased towards GC, is this not a problem?  I got 3 distinct segments, based on 200 bp windows, on methdiff object and after annotation all 3 segments are in promotor region and I am bit suspicious.  It is not finished yet but make a lot of questions in my head about this technique. Thank you for comments.  Marcin

RRBS is a problem because it is sparse. I wouldn't expect to get much out of it when used on methylBase objects.

For methylDiff objects, you get what I would expect, I think you didn't use any thresholding with getMethylDiff function. Since it is RRBS most of the segments you get will be on the promoter regions, most of the RRBS covered CpGs are on promoter regions. This will essentially spatially cluster DMCs based on their meth. difference similarity and proximity, which is what many tools that find DMRs with variable length are doing. 

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: 80f00f6e5c28f957
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] segmentation approach
parts:
Thank you Altuna for fast response.  I had tiled 200 bp, overdispersion removed by MN, 25% diff and qvalue=0.05.  I will try other combinations to see if I can make any sens from this fancy function. What is left unclear for me is what the bed graph actually produces. For the 3rd contrast, I have 3 segments in the same regions. I would expect that the one segment is covering unique regions.  If someone wants to try I noticed that eDMR package operates only on individual CpGs. It did not converged 200 tiled object from methylKit ... 

Aluna, I also wanted to ask, is it possible somehow to filter the annotated regions first before running differential methylation on these? (is it allowed, any function for this?). I tried to look for the function in methylKit but seems that annotation is done only after diffmeth object is created.

Would be nice with some workshop ... :-)

Many thanks,
Marcin

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] segmentation approach
parts:
I'm not sure why you would get overlapping segments this shouldn't happen. it might be due to tiling. We only tested this with CpGs not tiles. If you can send a reproducible example I can check if it is a bug or not.

You can filter CpGs and then run differential methylation. For filtering you can use findOverlaps family of functions from GenomicRanges package. methylKit objects can be coerced to GRanges to do overlap operations
http://compgenomr.github.io/book/genomic-intervals-and-r.html#operations-on-genomic-intervals-with-genomicranges-package

Best,
Altuna

Hi, 

My goal is to apply hclust to the dataset with only Differentially methylated positions.
In order to get methylBase object (like "meth") with only the differentially methylated CpGs ("alldiff"), I have followed the advises posted here:

> class(meth)
[1] "methylBase"
attr(,"package")
[1] "methylKit"
> class(alldiff)
[1] "data.frame"
> library(GenomicRanges)
> GRanges_alldiff<-as(alldiff,"GRanges")
> class(GRanges_alldiff)
[1] "GRanges"
attr(,"package")
[1] "GenomicRanges"
> GRanges_meth<-as(meth,"GRanges")

> overlapsFem<-findOverlaps(GRanges_meth,GRanges_alldiff)
> head(overlapsFem)

> overlappedMethAllFem<-meth[ as(meth,"GRanges") %over%  overlapsFem, ]
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘findOverlaps’ for signature ‘"GRanges", "SortedByQueryHits"’

#I have also tried by switching files for queryHits and subjectHits:
overlapsFem<-findOverlaps(GRanges_alldiff,GRanges_meth)

Is something wrong with the script/workflow, or my methylKit version is too old?

Thank you!

On 14 March 2017 at 20:55, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:

you need to do sth like the following to get a logical vector and feed that in []

methylBase.obj[ as(methylBase.obj,"GRanges") %over%  regionsOfInterest, ]
On Tue, Mar 14, 2017 at 3:56 PM, Gmail Marcin <marcin.b...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks! 

Once you get the subset of GRranges, I do not see the way of recreating from the GRanges object the methylKit object for further differential analysis.  Or did I missed something?

Cheers,
Marcin
On 14 March 2017 at 12:12, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:

I'm not sure why you would get overlapping segments this shouldn't happen. it might be due to tiling. We only tested this with CpGs not tiles. If you can send a reproducible example I can check if it is a bug or not.

You can filter CpGs and then run differential methylation. For filtering you can use findOverlaps family of functions from GenomicRanges package. methylKit objects can be coerced to GRanges to do overlap operations
http://compgenomr.github.io/book/genomic-intervals-and-r.html#operations-on-genomic-intervals-with-genomicranges-package

Best,
Altuna
On Tue, Mar 14, 2017 at 11:55 AM, Gmail Marcin <marcin.b...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thank you Altuna for fast response.  I had tiled 200 bp, overdispersion removed by MN, 25% diff and qvalue=0.05.  I will try other combinations to see if I can make any sens from this fancy function. What is left unclear for me is what the bed graph actually produces. For the 3rd contrast, I have 3 segments in the same regions. I would expect that the one segment is covering unique regions.  If someone wants to try I noticed that eDMR package operates only on individual CpGs. It did not converged 200 tiled object from methylKit ... 

Aluna, I also wanted to ask, is it possible somehow to filter the annotated regions first before running differential methylation on these? (is it allowed, any function for this?). I tried to look for the function in methylKit but seems that annotation is done only after diffmeth object is created.

Would be nice with some workshop ... :-)

Many thanks,
Marcin
On 14 March 2017 at 00:50, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Marcin,

.  I am bit confused the way it is applied though. Seems that you can use it for both diffmeth object or genomic ranges (ie methylome). Do I understand that correctly? 
 
Yes, if you apply it to DMCs, you would essentially get DMRs that do not have pre-defined lengths. I recommend using this on q-value thresholded DMCs, so no thresholding on methylation difference.  
 
The implication of the segmentation on these two different object is not intuitive to me. Theoretically you can compare different epigenomes (cells) based on that (make their signature) or run methyldiff function between two cell types, run the segmentation of this difference and do annotation. Are both approaches allowed? 

segmentation on methylBase objects is similar to the previous applications. You would essentially get 2 to 4 segment classes. the hypo-methylated or lowly methylated segment classes are probably regulatory regions. See Stadler et al. (2009) Nature.

If you run it on methylDiff objects thresholded by q-values, you should get DMRs. This would be similar to other DMR approaches such as eDMR package. 
 
Also, since RRBS is bit biased towards GC, is this not a problem?  I got 3 distinct segments, based on 200 bp windows, on methdiff object and after annotation all 3 segments are in promotor region and I am bit suspicious.  It is not finished yet but make a lot of questions in my head about this technique. Thank you for comments.  Marcin

RRBS is a problem because it is sparse. I wouldn't expect to get much out of it when used on methylBase objects.

For methylDiff objects, you get what I would expect, I think you didn't use any thresholding with getMethylDiff function. Since it is RRBS most of the segments you get will be on the promoter regions, most of the RRBS covered CpGs are on promoter regions. This will essentially spatially cluster DMCs based on their meth. difference similarity and proximity, which is what many tools that find DMRs with variable length are doing. 

Best,
Altuna
